Retrospective, non-interventional comparison of combat veterans with and without PTSD; MRI was conducted within one week of odor sampling.

value: Combat veterans with PTSD had significantly reduced gray matter volume in left anterior piriform cortex and right orbitofrontal cortex compared to combat veterans without PTSD; these differences remained significant after Bonferroni correction.

The findings extend established relationships between PTSD symptomatology and gray matter volume in fear-, threat-, and anxiety-associated structures by demonstrating PTSD-related volume decreases in primary and secondary olfactory cortex.

spans.text: Demonstrates that combat veterans with PTSD (CV + PTSD) compared to combat controls (CV-PTSD) had significantly reduced GMV in primary and secondary olfactory cortex (i.e., left anterior piriform and right orbitofrontal). These differences remained significant after Bonferroni correction for multiple brain region comparisons.

Data were preprocessed according to default toolbox settings: bias correction; tissue classification/segmentation ( Rajapakse et al., 1997 ); partial volume estimation ( Tohka et al., 2004 ); denoising/filtering ( Manjon et al., 2010 , Rajapakse et al., 1997 ); warping to the DARTEL IXI-550 template in Montreal Neurologic Institute (MNI) space; resampling to a 1.5 mm 3 voxel-size using high-dimensional affine and nonlinear transforms ( Ashburner, 2007 ); voxelwise modulation by nonlinear transform components only ( Ashburner and Friston, 2001 ); and finally, smoothing of normalized gray matter (GM) tissue maps with a 6 mm 3 FWHM Gaussian filter.

description.value: Participants sampled four odor cues and provided visual analog scale ratings of odor intensity, unpleasantness, and odor-elicited PTSD symptoms.

instructions.value: Participants sniffed each odor four times on a 6-second breathing cycle, consisting of a 3-second inhale and 3-second exhale.
